reviewTrigger: Public export, SDK, API, docs runtime, versioning, or release-stage change

journeys.startingState: Clean checkout with frozen Bun dependencies installed.
inputs: Repository calculator fixtures and canonical rule inputs
journeys.stepsOrProcedureOwner: bun run test; the retained test-check detail must name @taxkit/calculators as an executed workspace task
expectedBehavior: Calculator assertions produce the schema-backed tax results owned by the package.
preservedInvariants: No registry, provider, publication, or deployment operation.
journeys.oracle: The package tests exercise the public calculator implementation rather than an imitation fixture.
evidence: The test-check detail in the retained release attempt, including the @taxkit/calculators task outcome.
nonClaims: Local calculation tests do not prove a published package or external consumer.

journeys.boundary: Dist-only tarball and public SDK export paths
journeys.startingState: Clean checkout with SDK build inputs available.
journeys.stepsOrProcedureOwner: bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk check-packed-artifact then bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk validate:downstream
expectedBehavior: The dist-only tarball installs and every supported public entrypoint imports in the downstream consumer.
The installed plain client retains all three supported calculator results, closes its caller-owned lifetime and returns checked errors for later calls.
expectedSideEffects: Transient tarballs and a command-owned temporary consumer workspace.
preservedInvariants: Tarballs are deleted by their owning command and are never durable release evidence.
journeys.oracle: The consumer installs the actual packed artifact rather than importing workspace source.
journeys.environment: Local TaxKit checkout and isolated temporary consumer
evidence: Packed-artifact and downstream-consumer detail digests in the retained release attempt.
nonClaims: No npm publication, registry state, or external install is established.

journeys.boundary: Standalone local API health, metadata, calculation, schema failure, and OpenAPI contract
journeys.startingState: The standalone API app can start from the clean checkout.
inputs: Package-owned HTTP smoke requests and OpenAPI snapshot
expectedBehavior: Health, metadata, successful calculation, schema-error, and OpenAPI checks match the owning HTTP Schemas.
expectedSideEffects: An ephemeral local API process only.
preservedInvariants: No provider or deployed endpoint access.
journeys.oracle: The package-owned smoke client decodes real local HTTP responses with the canonical Schemas.
evidence: The api-smoke detail digest in the retained release attempt.
nonClaims: No deployed API or production behavior is established.

journeys.boundary: Local docs content, built SSR, hydration, HTTP status, navigation, server-function, recoverable-error, and console behavior
journeys.startingState: Docs dependencies and the repository browser runtime are available locally.
journeys.stepsOrProcedureOwner: bun run docs:validate then bun run --filter=docs test:browser then bun run --filter=docs test:built
expectedBehavior: Validated content renders in the generated production app, the initial response contains the requested MDX, hydration is diagnostic-free, real sidebar and authored-MDX links cross the server-function transport without a document reload, client navigation restores heading focus without stealing initial hydration focus, keyboard/landmark/current-navigation/contrast/reduced-motion assertions pass, expected failures remain recoverable, and missing pages return HTTP 404 with framework-native not-found UI.
expectedSideEffects: Transient local build/browser output only, plus the bounded DAR-013 PNG/manifest set when the separately invoked candidate-bound screenshot mode is authorized.
preservedInvariants: No network publication or deployed-site mutation.
journeys.oracle: Direct HTTP assertions establish SSR body and 404 status before Playwright independently observes hydration, server-function requests, zero document requests during real internal navigation, focus/keyboard/landmark/contrast/motion behavior, pending, not-found and error/console states; candidate-bound screenshots are supplemental only.
evidence: The docs-validation and docs-browser detail digests in the retained release attempt.
For DOCS-APP-006 only, the completed execution plan's candidate-bound DAR-013 PNG/manifest set after primary-owner visual review.
nonClaims: Local built/browser proof does not establish deployment, provider routing, a public URL, production behavior, or public availability.
A screenshot does not prove HTTP status, SSR response content, hydration diagnostics, request type, keyboard/focus behavior, contrast, motion suppression or console cleanliness.

journeys.boundary: One ordered local release-readiness attempt and its sanitized retained details
journeys.startingState: A candidate checkout has an exact base commit, changed-content digest, and pending Changesets state.
expectedBehavior: All nine checks execute once in order and success is reported only with true zero exits and addressable sanitized detail digests.
expectedSideEffects: Ignored command-owned sanitized detail files under tmp/release-readiness only.
preservedInvariants: Presentation never reruns a completed or failed attempt.
Failed and inconclusive provenance is retained.
journeys.oracle: The runtime decodes the inventory and proof packet at filesystem ingress, preserves true terminal states, and rejects missing or mismatched evidence.
evidence: The release attempt detail paths/digests and candidate proof packet.
nonClaims: Local closure is not approval for a tag, release, npm publication, deployment, provider access, or public availability.

journeys.actorOrConsumer: Calculator Website visitor and documentation reader
journeys.boundary: Built and live native Website/private API binding/direct browser RPC
journeys.startingState: Selected Node and Chromium are available; local ports 4196–4205 used by the native fixtures are available.
inputs: Native Alchemy source-built API and Website
Retained take-home example: 1654 dollars weekly, threshold claimed
Retained withholding example: 9500 dollars monthly, threshold not claimed
Retained annual example: 67000 dollars taxable income
Accepted 61-page documentation catalogue and matching compiled MDX presentation
expectedBehavior: Initial rendering makes no calculation; explicit Calculate produces 1301 dollars take-home pay through the private binding and direct browser POST /rpc.

Idle settings remain available; repeated Worker calls finish; editing cancels unfinished work and keeps the previous successful answer visibly out of date until a successful explicit calculation; the form also works without JavaScript.
Checked errors restore safely in the browser; native request limits and production import boundaries hold.
Data-free native settings GET succeeds; unexpected query/method input is rejected before framework parsing; an actual internal settings defect returns empty 500 and fixed safe logs.
Unknown, extended or missing native settings function addresses return empty 404 before framework lookup/logging; native generated URL owns identity.
Controlled slow headers and an unfinished actual reply reach the ten-second deadline; browser requests abort after the deadline, editing and browser Back leaving the form.
Real native CLI local development supplies both addresses/bindings, reloads API and Website source, restores exact sources and closes app ports on scoped shutdown.
Both actual saved local resources have explicitly disabled platform log/trace collection and zero sampling; source restoration uses the non-polling watcher and requires both visible page updates.
Take-home explanation opens with the keyboard without calculation; breakdown, recorded threshold and rule sources remain attached to the old report after form edits.

Catalogue-backed navigation offers all three calculators; withholding and annual pages start with their own empty result and return the retained 2756 and 12228 dollar answers through real browser RPC and standard HTML POST without JavaScript.
The new pages retain their own report and explanation after edits without another request; the annual Medicare limitation stays visible and the agent route links to actual API descriptions.

All supported native HTML form POST paths and public HTTP/RPC reject more than 64 KiB of encoded text with fixed safe HTML 413 form guidance or checked JSON 413 API guidance; public rejection preserves the Website CORS policy.
All nine closed named calculator RPC calls return checked canonical results; the seven additional metadata calls run through the real built API Worker.
Reached metadata work times out at five seconds through both actual HTTP and the generated RPC client; HTTP 504 keeps CORS and safe cleanup is observed. Metadata takes no calculation place.
All 61 accepted pages return real SSR articles with matching headings, navigation, title, description, canonical and checked Markdown link; missing public pages return native HTML 404.

Native data-free documentation GET accepts only bounded public page headers; original SSR addresses cannot be overridden by headers. Invalid query/content-type/page inputs reject before framework parsing.

Cold body/metadata/module mismatch and damaged native browser transport show safe recoverable guidance. Internal sidebar/authored links use native GET without document reload, with one current-page marker and deliberate heading focus; hydration preserves initial focus.
Mobile navigation and table scrolling work with the keyboard, horizontal content stays inside the article and ordinary documentation links work without JavaScript.

The accepted-catalogue search form retains literal URL words and Unicode, checks duplicate/unknown keys and bounded native URI headers, distinguishes empty/no-match/unavailable states and uses safe recoverable damaged-transport guidance.
Search native navigation retains the document; actual standard GET submission and result links work without JavaScript, with keyboard focus and contained phone layout.
After printed local addresses, served-page readiness retries only 502/503 for at most fifteen seconds; actual browser navigation still requires 200 and its expected heading.

Four conventional discovery files derive from the accepted catalogue and checked stage origins through the private API client; actual GET/HEAD headers and bodies, XML parsing, all canonical addresses and safe unavailable/method/query responses hold.
expectedSideEffects: Ignored native build files, scoped local Workers and Chromium only.
preservedInvariants: Retained tax results and existing docs operations stay unchanged.
No provider, state, credentials, deployment or publication operation.
journeys.oracle: Actual native built artifacts run in workerd; real Chromium independently confirms the exact RPC endpoint, no initial/replayed call, no trace/cookie headers and the retained answer. The API artifact contains the engine marker while browser artifacts must not. The generated native settings identity, short request marker and source-built internal defect require actual responses and positive fixed reporting; removing the owning failure boundary makes marker reflection fail the saved test. Unknown native function-address requests must return empty 404 and must omit the short request marker from actual native logs; removing exact-address admission restores that log leak. Actual built API global/procedure/fatal replies use fixed safe values; expected/version errors retain checked identity. A source-built damaged valid-JSON reply must restore a checked error through the genuine Website binding, with real Chromium editing and no replay. Positive fixed host logs omit the marker and pay values. Removal of each native encoder or the owned reply decoder must fail the saved test, followed by exact restoration and fresh dependency/artifact builds. Controlled API roots retain the real calculation/encoding and delay headers or the remaining body for twelve seconds. Actual generated clients must hit the ten-second deadline; Chromium must observe request abort after deadline, editing and actual Back route departure. Removing deadline or edit interruption fails the saved test; exact restoration and fresh builds pass. Pay-value checks inspect emitted log messages; private text checks inspect the whole record. Actual native mock-plan properties and saved real CLI state must contain the disabled collection policy; removing the API graph property fails the saved state Schema after runtime checks. These are declared-state checks, not cloud upload or exported-row proof. An actual successful browser answer survives edits, controlled unavailable retry and invalid form without being presented as current. Reverting figures makes no request and still needs one explicit real RPC to clear the stale message. Actual Worker-generated successful submission HTML hydrates without replay and retains its answer through editing and failed retry. The additional pages must independently return both known results via real API artifacts; no calculation fixture supplies them. Each page starts without the previous calculator's answer. Saved forms and report identity are checked together. Exact browser locator fill admissions have actual CLI positive and neighbouring-application negative fixtures. The size oracle uses multi-byte text below 65536 characters but above 65536 encoded bytes at both API paths and all three form paths. API boundary fixtures also accept exactly 65536 bytes and reject progressive streams without reading their tail. The bounded private client must classify an actual native 413 as the checked request-size error. Valid native calculator/catalogue replies at exactly 2 MiB succeed; over-limit streams stop before the tail and release. Status fixtures prove request-controller abort, safe serialized guidance and one call only. Six restored checked error variants hydrate with their guidance and no new calculation. The built shared-work fixture reaches eight calculations across one HTTP call and a seven-item RPC batch, refuses extra HTTP/SSR/public browser work, retains manual-retry guidance with no edit replay, emits checked HTTP 504/RPC timeouts at five seconds and reaches cleanup. The actual generated client preserves timeout identity. Direct scoped tests prove cancelled/failed place reuse and independent instance pools; timers do not claim forced CPU pre-emption. The owning native pair also reads detail/schema/graph/facts/rules/jurisdictions/tax years from the actual API artifact. The shared RPC corpus proves decoder, size, status, deadline, interruption and old-revision rejection for every named call. Documentation assertions inspect actual initial HTML for every page before independent Chromium navigation. Three source-built API variants retain valid checked pages but change Markdown, metadata or module identity; cold Website SSR and the actual native GET must detect each mismatch. A genuine server-function response is damaged in the browser to prove restoration rejects it. The API artifact must positively contain the executable calculator service identity and browser chunks must omit it; accepted documentation prose cannot stand in for an engine marker. Full-page images supplement functional observations only. Search SSR titles must match real built API results; the original URL resists a forged header. Native function identity is read from its compiled owner. A damaged genuine search reply must fail restoration. Actual form/result navigation and JavaScript-free submission are independently observed in Chromium. Focused browser navigation waits for rendered words before asserting checked outcomes; a bare router promise is insufficient. Bounded startup readiness cannot hide application errors or a persistent gateway failure. Actual built discovery GET bodies must equal the checked native client documents. Chromium XML parsing must produce the sitemap namespace and all 61 canonical addresses in catalogue order. Explicit HEAD 200 must have an empty body and GET-equivalent headers. A real unavailable API binding must return empty uncached 503. The actual RPC corpus rejects a valid document for a different requested path.
journeys.environment: Local TaxKit checkout, native workerd and Chromium
nonClaims: No cloud provider, deployed endpoint or trace-export proof; controlled native fatal/privacy paths are qualified only by the named local tests.
Public and private API requests use separate local isolates from the same API artifact; caller upload cancellation is not established.
Browser/caller abort does not establish cancellation of the upstream artificial delayed Worker response.
